Here's what the search turned up on avoiding a loading fallback for `searchParams`-dependent content with Cache Components:

## The core mechanism: `<Link prefetch={true}>` + Partial Prefetching

The default prefetch doesn't cover URL-specific data. The shared App Shell does not include URL data that varies by destination, such as searchParams and params. Setting `prefetch={true}` on a link resolves cached content that depends on its URL data before navigation instead of streaming that content after navigation.With `<Link prefetch={true}>` pointing at a Partial Prefetching route, Next.js renders that route's component tree again at prefetch time, this time with the destination URL resolved — so more of the tree resolves now that its searchParams and params are in scope: `use cache` called with values extracted from runtime APIs (passed as arguments) joins the per-link prefetch, `use cache: private` executes on the server and caches the result in the browser as part of the per-link prefetch, and `<Suspense>` fallbacks stay in the prefetched UI while uncached content streams at request time.



The payoff: on the click, the results render immediately with no fallback — the prerender advances through anything static or cached, then stops at uncached reads and falls back to the surrounding `<Suspense>` boundary, which is already in place from structuring the route for instant navigation.

## Required config
This assumes Cache Components with `partialPrefetching` enabled:

```ts
// next.config.ts
const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
  cacheComponents: true,
  partialPrefetching: true,
}
```
The destination must use Partial Prefetching, enabled globally with `partialPrefetching` or per segment with `prefetch = 'partial'`.

## The code pattern

Never read `searchParams` inside the cached scope. You cannot call `cookies()`, `headers()`, `searchParams`, or other dynamic APIs inside a cached scope. Read them first and pass only the serializable value a cached function needs. URL-dependent reads marked with `'use cache'` can then be included in that link's prefetch, so a product or detail page arrives with its content ready.

You still need the boundary: like `searchParams`, `params` needs a `<Suspense>` boundary, even when the values are predefined by `generateStaticParams`. The trick is that the fallback simply never becomes visible once the prefetch resolves.

## When it's *not* worth it

Generating the per-link prefetch costs a server invocation per prefetchable link, so it is opt-in per link. You pay per visible link, regardless of click-through. Skip it when the route has little or no URL-data dependency, the App Shell already makes the navigation instant, the dependent content has to be fresh on every request (the prerender stops at the same `<Suspense>` fallback, so the user sees the same UI either way), or the route is rarely navigated to.

Two caveats worth planning around:
- A cold cache (first visit, or after expiration) means the server still has to compute the cached result, so users may see a loading spinner on that first navigation; subsequent navigations are instant as long as the cache is warm.
- A per-link prefetch is best-effort.

## Debugging
Because prefetching is disabled in development, it's hard to see what a user actually sees mid-navigation — the Navigation Inspector pauses page loads and client-side navigations at the shell so you can inspect the exact loading state. Cache Components also validates navigations, giving you insights and errors that guide you toward instant navigation — e.g. wrap data in `<Suspense>`, cache it with `use cache`, or move where the access happens.

Primary source: [Optimizing prefetching](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) and [Caching](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/caching) in the Next.js docs.

Everything inside the scope shares the same lifetime. Some subtrees are expensive enough to produce that you would rather not pay for them on every prefetch of the route. Awaiting [`unstable_navigation()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/navigation) above the work leaves it out of every prefetch, so it is produced on the navigation. Only the ranking is left out, and it keeps its cache lifetime. Without it, keeping a subtree out of a prefetch means leaving it uncached, which gives up that lifetime on the navigation too. Awaiting `unstable_navigation()` inside a cached scope is not allowed, so put the caching directive on a function called below it, as `rank` does here. For a subtree that would otherwise sit in the App Shell, but that a `` should still resolve before the click, use [`unstable_prefetch()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/prefetch) instead. ## Trade-offs Use `prefetch={true}` on routes where: - Part of the component tree depends on URL data: the full URL, `searchParams`, or `params` not resolved by [`generateStaticParams`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-static-params) - That part of the tree has a known cache lifetime (it can be expressed with `"use cache"` or `"use cache: private"`) - The traffic justifies the per-link server invocation Skip it when the prefetch can't produce a better UI than the App Shell. On a slow connection, on a feed of many links, or on a direct visit, it may not be ready when the user navigates, and the navigation falls back to the App Shell. When many links to a route are visible at once, such as a grid of cards, each `` prefetches that link's content as it enters the viewport, so the grid makes one such server request per card. Prefetch on intent instead. A [hover-triggered prefetch](/docs/app/guides/prefetching#hover-triggered-prefetch) fetches only the links the user is likely to click. The default `` (without `prefetch={true}`) prefetches only the App Shell, so it doesn't carry this cost. | | App Shell | Per-link prefetch with `prefetch={true}` | | ------- | ------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- | | Scope | One per route | One per visible `` | | Content | Route's rendered output minus per-link data | Same, plus per-link URL data resolved | | Cost | Bounded by route count | Bounded by visible-link count | | Role | Default prefetch | More rendered before click | [Excluding content](#exclude-content-from-a-prefetch) is one more control on top of these. The trade is generating content for a prefetch that may never be used, against momentarily showing a `` fallback while that content streams in. ## Next steps - [Adopting Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching) for how `` behaves under the new model and how to migrate existing apps. - [`prefetch` API reference](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/prefetch) for all prefetch modes. - [`use cache: private` reference](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-private) for per-user caching specifics. - [`unstable_prefetch()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/prefetch) and [`unstable_navigation()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/navigation) for the full behavior of each prefetch stage. - [Instant navigation guide](/docs/app/guides/instant-navigation) for validating the route's caching structure. - [Caching](/docs/app/getting-started/caching) for background on `use cache`, Suspense, and Partial Prerendering.

title: partialPrefetching
description: Configure the default link prefetch behavior to fetch only the static parts of each route.

---

`partialPrefetching` enables Partial Prefetching at the app level. The framework prefetches the static parts of each route by default; set `prefetch={true}` on individual links to use [per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) and fetch more.

## Usage

```ts filename="next.config.ts" highlight={5} switcher
import type { NextConfig } from 'next'

const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
  cacheComponents: true,
  partialPrefetching: true,
}

export default nextConfig
```

```js filename="next.config.js" highlight={3} switcher
module.exports = {
  cacheComponents: true,
  partialPrefetching: true,
}
```

`partialPrefetching` requires [`cacheComponents`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents). Without it, `next dev` and `next build` throw at config validation.

## Reference

| Value   | Description                                 |
| ------- | ------------------------------------------- |
| `true`  | Enables Partial Prefetching across the app. |
| `false` | Default. No change to prefetch behavior.    |

## How prefetches resolve

Before Partial Prefetching, Next.js prefetched per visible link: a page with N links to N routes produced ~N route prefetches as those links entered the viewport.

With `partialPrefetching: true`, Next.js prefetches one reusable [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell) per route instead. The App Shell contains rendered output that does not depend on a link's URL. URL-specific content, including content that depends on `params` or `searchParams`, resolves after navigation by default. App Shells are cached on the client, so links to the same route reuse one prefetch.

The pattern is similar to per-route code splitting in single-page apps: one artifact per route, shared by every link that points to it.

> **Good to know**: Routes that read `cookies()` or `headers()` produce an App Shell that includes session data. The framework auto-detects this and caches the shell per session on the client.

A link can ask for more than the App Shell with [`<Link prefetch={true}>`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link#prefetch). The prefetch also resolves URL data like `params`, `searchParams`, and the full URL, and the cached content behind it. See [Optimizing prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching).

> **Good to know**: If you use `<Link prefetch={true}>` to a route that hasn't opted into Partial Prefetching, a dev console error suggests enabling `partialPrefetching` app-wide or `prefetch = 'partial'` on the segment. The [dev warning Insight](/docs/messages/instant-link-prefetch-partial) covers each fix in detail.

## Per-segment overrides

A segment that exports an explicit [`prefetch`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/prefetch) value overrides the app-level default for that route.

## Version History

| Version | Change                                                                     |
| ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 16.3.0  | `partialPrefetching` introduced. Requires `cacheComponents` to be enabled. |

Done. The `/catalog?category=...` URLs are unchanged; the category-specific heading and product list are now resolved at prefetch time.

## Changes

**`next.config.ts`** — enabled Partial Prefetching alongside Cache Components:
```ts
cacheComponents: true,
partialPrefetching: true,
```
By default a `<Link>` prefetches one reusable App Shell per route, which deliberately excludes URL data like `searchParams` — that's why `/catalog` always showed its fallback on click.

**`app/page.tsx`** — opted each category link into a per-link prefetch with `prefetch={true}`, so Next renders `/catalog` again at prefetch time with that link's `category` in scope.

**`app/catalog/page.tsx`** — gave the URL-dependent read a cache lifetime so the prefetch prerender can advance past it instead of stopping at the Suspense boundary:
```tsx
async function getCategoryProducts(category: string) {
  'use cache'
  return getProducts(category)
}
```
`searchParams` is still read outside the cached scope (you can't call it inside one) and only the plain `category` string crosses the boundary, so the cache entry is keyed per category. The `<Suspense>` boundary stays — it's still required for `searchParams`, it just never becomes visible once the prefetch resolves. The heading needed no change; it derives synchronously from `category`, which the prefetch already knows.

## Verified against a production build

`next build` reports "Partial Prefetching enabled" and `/catalog` as a Partial Prerender route. Against `next start`, comparing the two prefetch kinds for `?category=sale`:

| Prefetch | Payload contains | Time |
|---|---|---|
| App Shell (route-shared) | `Loading category` only | 12 ms |
| Per-link (`prefetch={true}`) | `Products on sale`, `Canvas Tote`, `Travel Mug` | 851 ms cold → **10 ms warm** |

`?category=featured` behaves the same with its own heading and items (`Desk Lamp`, `Wool Blanket`). The click itself does no server render — it reads the already-resolved prefetch — so the fallback never shows once the prefetch lands.

Two caveats worth knowing: prefetching is disabled in `next dev`, so this only shows up in a production build; and a cold cache (first visit or after expiry) still pays the ~800 ms, so the very first navigation can flash the fallback. Currently `getCategoryProducts` uses the default `cacheLife` profile — if you want a specific staleness window for the catalog, add a `cacheLife(...)` call there.

I also reverted the formatting churn `next build` wrote into `tsconfig.json` to keep the diff focused; it'll rewrite it on your next build. The pre-existing `package.json` pin was left as-is.

Sources: [Optimizing prefetching](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching), [`partialPrefetching`](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching) (read from the version-matched docs in `node_modules/next/dist/docs/`).
